article.title: Why an A/B Test Needs a Stable Population
article.why: 把 randomization、population shift、external validity 與 stratification 串在一起，適合數據分析與實驗設計學習。
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

paragraphs.en:
An A/B test is designed to isolate the effect of an intervention, but random assignment is not enough if the population itself changes in important ways during the experiment. A treatment and control group can be perfectly randomized at the start and still produce a result that is difficult to generalize when traffic composition, eligibility rules, product exposure, or user behavior shifts while the test is running.

Consider an online campaign tested for four weeks. In the first two weeks, most visitors are existing customers. In the final two weeks, a promotion brings in many new users. If new users have a very different baseline conversion rate, the overall average can move even when the treatment effect within each type of user is stable. Randomization protects the comparison between treatment and control inside the observed sample, but it does not guarantee that the sample represents the population you care about next month.

This distinction is important because analysts often mix two questions. The first is causal: did the treatment change outcomes for the people included in the experiment? The second is external: should we expect the same effect when the treatment is rolled out to a broader or future population? Randomization helps strongly with the first question. The second requires attention to population stability and effect heterogeneity.

A practical check is to compare the composition of traffic over time. Analysts can track device type, geography, customer tenure, acquisition channel, prior activity, model score, or other pre-treatment characteristics. The goal is not to test every variable mechanically. It is to identify factors that are both related to the outcome and likely to change the treatment effect. If the share of high-value customers suddenly falls, an overall conversion rate may change even if the experiment is behaving normally.

Stratified randomization can help when an important characteristic is known in advance. For example, if a campaign is expected to behave differently for high-, medium-, and low-score customers, treatment and control can be randomized within each score band. This keeps the groups balanced and makes subgroup estimates easier to interpret. However, stratification does not solve every future shift. If the business later sends the campaign to a completely different population, the original estimate may still need adjustment.

Time effects also matter. Weekends, holidays, salary dates, product launches, and competitor actions can change user behavior. Because treatment and control run at the same time, many common time shocks cancel in the difference. The problem appears when treatment exposure interacts with time or when the mix of users changes across periods. Analysts should therefore avoid comparing a treatment group from one period with a control group from another unless the design explicitly accounts for time.

Monitoring does not mean repeatedly checking the p-value and stopping when the result looks favorable. That practice can inflate false positives. Population monitoring is different: it asks whether the experiment is still operating under the conditions that make the estimate meaningful. The analysis plan should define the sample, treatment, outcome window, and important segmentation before results are interpreted.

After the test, report both the overall treatment effect and the context in which it was measured. If effects differ materially by segment, a weighted rollout estimate may be more useful than one unqualified average. For example, a future campaign aimed mostly at high-score customers should not automatically use the average effect from a test dominated by medium-score customers.

The broader lesson is that an experiment estimates an effect for a particular population under particular conditions. Randomization creates a fair comparison; it does not freeze the business environment. Stable definitions, concurrent controls, composition checks, and subgroup analysis help analysts distinguish a real change in treatment impact from a change in who happened to enter the experiment.
paragraphs.zh:
A/B test 的目的，是把某個 intervention 的因果影響隔離出來，但如果實驗期間 population 本身發生重要變化，random assignment 並不足以保證結果能直接套用到未來。Treatment 和 control 在起點可以完全隨機化，但 traffic composition、eligibility、product exposure 或 user behavior 若在實驗期間改變，最終平均效果可能很難 generalize。

例如一個四週 campaign，前兩週大多是既有客，後兩週因促銷帶來大量新客。如果新客 baseline CVR 與既有客差很多，即使 treatment effect 在每一類人內都很穩定，overall average 仍可能改變。Randomization 能保護 observed sample 內的 treatment-control 比較，卻不能保證這個 sample 代表下個月真正要 rollout 的 population。

因此要區分兩個問題：第一是 causal question——這次 treatment 是否改變了參與者結果；第二是 external question——未來擴大到更廣 population 時，效果是否仍一樣。Randomization 對第一個問題很強，但第二個問題還要看 population stability 與 effect heterogeneity。

實務上可以持續比較 traffic composition，例如 device、geography、customer tenure、acquisition channel、prior activity、model score 等 pre-treatment characteristics。目的不是機械式地檢驗每個變數，而是找出同時與 outcome 有關、且可能改變 treatment effect 的因素。若 high-value customers 比例突然下降，overall CVR 可能改變，即使 experiment 本身運作正常。

若重要分群在實驗前就知道，可以採 stratified randomization。例如高、中、低模型分數各自進行 treatment/control 隨機化，有助於維持平衡並解讀 subgroup estimates。但 stratification 也不能解決所有未來 population shift；若未來 rollout 對象完全不同，仍需要重新加權或重新驗證。

時間效果也重要。週末、假日、發薪日、產品 launch 或競爭對手活動都可能改變 user behavior。同期 treatment/control 可以抵消很多共同 time shock，但如果 treatment exposure 與時間互動、或不同期間 population mix 改變，就仍可能出問題。因此不要拿不同時期的 treatment 和 control 直接比較，除非設計有明確處理 time effect。

Monitoring population composition 不等於每天看 p-value、看到顯著就停止。後者可能提高 false positive；前者是在確認實驗是否仍運行於可解讀的條件中。Sample、treatment、outcome window 與重要 segmentation 最好在看結果前先定義。

最後報告時，除了 overall treatment effect，也應交代測量時的 population context。若 segment effect 明顯不同，針對未來 rollout population 做 weighted estimate，可能比單一平均更有用。核心概念是：實驗估計的是特定 population、特定條件下的效果。Randomization 建立公平比較，但不會凍結商業環境；stable definition、concurrent control、composition check 與 subgroup analysis 才能幫助你區分「效果真的變了」和「進入實驗的人變了」。
paragraphs.ja:
A/Bテストは施策の因果効果を分離するためのものですが、実験中にpopulation自体が変化すると、random assignmentだけでは将来への一般化を保証できません。開始時にtreatmentとcontrolを完全にランダム化しても、traffic composition、eligibility、product exposure、user behaviorが変われば、結果の意味が変わることがあります。

例えば四週間のcampaignで、前半は既存顧客が中心、後半はpromotionにより新規顧客が急増したとします。新規顧客のbaseline CVRが大きく異なる場合、各segment内のtreatment effectが安定していてもoverall averageは動きます。Randomizationは観測sample内の比較を守りますが、来月rolloutするpopulationを代表しているとは限りません。

ここではcausal questionとexternal questionを分けます。前者は今回の対象者に施策効果があったか、後者は将来より広いpopulationでも同じ効果を期待できるかです。前者にはrandomizationが強く、後者にはpopulation stabilityとeffect heterogeneityの確認が必要です。

実務ではdevice、地域、customer tenure、acquisition channel、prior activity、model scoreなどpre-treatment characteristicsの構成を時系列で確認します。すべてを機械的に検定するのではなく、outcomeと関係し、かつeffectを変えそうな要因に注目します。

重要なcharacteristicが事前に分かる場合はstratified randomizationが有効です。高・中・低scoreの各層でtreatment/controlをrandomizeすればbalanceを保ちやすく、subgroup estimateも解釈しやすくなります。ただし将来のpopulationが大きく変われば、元のestimateをそのまま使えない場合があります。

週末、祝日、給料日、product launch、competitor actionなどtime effectにも注意します。同時期のtreatment/controlなら共通shockは差分で消えやすいですが、population mixが期間ごとに変わる場合は問題が残ります。

Population monitoringはp-valueを何度も見て有利なところで止めることとは違います。前者はestimateが意味を持つ条件が維持されているかを見る作業です。sample、treatment、outcome window、主要segmentationは事前に決める方がよいでしょう。

結論として、実験は特定population・特定条件での効果を推定します。Randomizationは公平な比較を作りますが、business environmentを固定しません。stable definition、concurrent control、composition check、subgroup analysisを組み合わせることで、施策効果の変化と参加者構成の変化を区別しやすくなります。

vocabulary.usage: The target population can change over time.
A result may not generalize to future users.
New users may have a different baseline conversion rate.
Use stratified randomization across score bands.
A weighted rollout estimate may be more useful.
Population shifts can reduce external validity.

quiz.question: What does randomization protect?
quiz.answer: It protects the treatment-control comparison within the observed experiment sample.

quiz.question: Why can a population shift matter?
quiz.answer: Because the overall result may change when user composition or subgroup effects differ.

quiz.question: Output: Name one pre-treatment characteristic you would monitor.
quiz.answer: Example: model score or customer tenure.
